questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go somewhere I had a connection to. Somewhere I knew someone, so a country where I would already have contacts. I also wanted to choose somewhere with good academic opportunities and where I would be able to travel easily, I.E. where I could communicate with people easily. I had been in the Netherlands before and knew I enjoyed my trip there. I have good dutch friends too.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was easy! There was plenty of information online about practical matters such as Dutch systems and transport. Leiden university were also very good at providing online information about what to expect upon arrival.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I stayed at a student accomodation where there were other students able to help us with general information. Additionally, the university of Leiden had planned an option "introduction week" for new students. As I participated in this we got a lot of information both about the university and the city.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy for me since it was close to the city center. It would have been nice to have been provided an extra route guide on which buses etc. stopped nearby but with map apps it was pretty easy.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: If you're able to it's a good way to feel more integrated with the place you're living. Even if you still live in studen accommodations, it helps center your daily routines away from the university itself. I think it helps encourage you to explore the place you're staying more, and to get closer to how the natives live there as well.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Students should be aware that in provided housing standards might not be quite as high as they're used to if they're super cleanly or orderly themselves. It's definitely manageable, you can clean, and make it nice but it won't be the same as at home. That doesn't mean the housing isn't good! It's just temporary. Many people go through there.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: For Leiden university they let temporary exchange students pick through a separate system compared to how regular students do. You're on a much simpler platform and are able to wish between classes. You're informed through that platform if there's space for you on the course or if you need to apply for more courses. You can find available courses in their course catalogue and are guided on how to do that by university reps in online meetings before the exchange begins.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We were able to write the exchange office if we had any questions or problems. I was in contact with them multiple times and they were always very helpful. They also plan a few online meetings and presentations for incoming exchange students to give out general information and allow people to ask questions.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got rejected from a few of the classes I wanted initially because of a lack in availability for those courses. However, the other ones I ended up taking were also very interesting and I enjoyed them immensely.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be quick! Overall I believe that if you apply for something early then you're more likely to get it at Leiden. That goes both for classes and housing. Other than that you just have to keep yourself updated on the process so you can react if you need to reapply for something. It's also very easy to ask for help or ask questions if you're unsure of something.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took courses primarily at year 1 and 2 levels, one third year level. Like in UCPH a bachelor is three years long normally. The quality of the courses are very high. I wouldn't say any of them were difficult to follow if you're an active student but you don't need to worry about taking 1st year courses. They're still going to be interesting for you I think.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There are multiple different variations of teaching at Leiden university. The lectures are generally less interactive than they are at UCPH. A professor might ask a few questions but some ask basically none at all. It greatly depends. "work group" or discussion group classes are very active. They're not like the work groups we're used to where you can choose to participate. It's necessary for most of them that you show up ready to participate in dialogue and should be aware of this.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:

History of the Netherlands, Cultuurwetenschap I
Cultural Memory of World War I & II
Culture and Society of the Netherlands: An Inside
View Course
History of Modern Philosophy
Art and Self in the Age of Consumerism

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Dutch painting course was incredibly interesting if you want to learn more about art and dutch culture in general. It was designed to be at a level where you could participate even if you aren't an art history student and very interesting. I also really enjoyed the Big Media and History of Modern Philosophy courses. Both of them are more introductory and accessible to everyone but with very interesting material and great teachers/professors.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The housing was pretty sparse when i first moved in so there were quite a few essentials which needed to be bought. Cleaning supplies and basic interior like towels, etc. If you move into a student accommodation I think you should expect to spend at least some money on these things.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was cheaper than i expected. Compared to Denmark the stores are slightly cheaper, but the dutch also have weekly or bi-weekly markets where you can buy groceries. These are quite a bit cheaper and the food is fresh. If you're good at shopping at the markets you can save money. Eating out is also quite a lot cheaper than in denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are multiple clubs you can join at Leiden university even if just for a time. There's also a university sports center where you can either use the gym or attend sports.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The city of Leiden have a lot of activities that happen in the city around the year. Festivals and celebrations of any kind. I would recommend exchange students participate in Dutch festivals if they hear about them.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I would recommend traveling. The Netherlands are beautiful, even the parts that people don't usually go to. Even if transport costs a bit, the trains and public transport is easy to navigate and different cities have a lot of different things to offer.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy. It's similar enough to Denmark for you to adjust quickly but different enough to be interesting.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Speak to people in your classes. If you can chat with the people sitting next to you, you might get to know someone new. Especially if you're taking classes mostly attended by Dutch students, make an effort to get to know people there.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: You have to speak up in stores and in general. I'm a quiet person but you learn to ask for help or to claim your space. It's not about rudeness but rather about making it clear when you need help.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The Dutch people are generally very friendly and welcoming. It was really nice to see people interacting so much and getting to be part of that. The market culture and the speciality stores like grocery stores or butchers mean you go out between people more and makes life feel very active and connected.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Look for housing early! It's difficult to find and you want to be first on the list. Enjoy the courses you're taking and soak in what you can learn. The academic level is very high and the professors experts in their fields. Take advantage of the fact that you can study at other faculties than just your own. Go see the different buildings, libraries, and the botanical garden.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Even if you don't have friends that are going there, don't worry. There's a lot of exchange and foreign students at Leiden university, so even if you're considering going alone, you will be able to make new friends there. They might just be really good friends too!

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Leiden university is very old, with history back to the 1500-hundreds, and it was amazing to attend a university that old and storied. Even most of the buildings are newer, you can really feel that it's an institution of academic renown and the level of education goes along with that.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I had some personal difficulties while being away. A parent undergoing a big surgery while I was in a different country. It was hard to concentrate during the time that was going on but I tried my best to enjoy the experience anyway.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
